subject.title: [Bug]: Agents should not be able to access or modify files outside their own working space.

question: Should OpenClaw make per-agent workspace containment the default security boundary for host filesystem tools, or keep unrestricted host access as the default and require an explicit sandbox/workspaceOnly configuration?
rationale: The source shows opt-in containment exists, but changing the default or adding a hard boundary affects security posture, existing host-access workflows, and compatibility with skills and tool execution.

options.title: Make workspace containment default
options.body: Adopt a secure-by-default boundary, provide migration/doctor guidance for trusted host access, and require tests covering file tools plus exec/sandbox interactions.

options.title: Keep current default with better setup UX
options.body: Preserve unrestricted host access by default but make setup/doctor/docs strongly guide users to workspaceOnly, sandbox, SSH, or local-user isolation for multi-agent deployments.

options.title: Close into a broader sandbox tracker
options.body: Treat this report as covered only after a protected sandbox/isolation tracker has an accepted design and this issue's concrete PM-agent workspace collision is linked there.

recommendation.title: Make workspace containment default
recommendation.body: Adopt a secure-by-default boundary, provide migration/doctor guidance for trusted host access, and require tests covering file tools plus exec/sandbox interactions.

likelyOwner.reason: Their protected local-user sandbox issue is the most concrete maintainer-facing direction for the same per-agent workspace/account boundary problem.
